I thought I’d be all artsy and use Apple cider vinegar cause it was brown. So I poured the apple cider vinegar in to a Tupperware container. Then I cut cucumbers in to long wedges - telling my mom I was doing so because of course it would help accelerate the process (thought I was being a genius). And I placed the long wedges in the vinegar.

Mom asked how long I would leave the container in the fridge. I replied “How long? Why? It shouldn’t take long for these to become pickles. Probably over night.” Then I closed the fridge and went on my merry way.

As kids will do, I forgot all about my “pickles” until Mom reminded me of them maybe a week later when I dragged myself out of bed. “Oh yeah!”, I exclaimed, “Let’s try them out!” Thinking that eating pickles first thing in the morning would be awesome, naturally.

So I went to the fridge, got out the container, selected one particularly fat cucumber spear, and took a huge bite.

I don’t think I’ve seen my Mom laugh that hard. She laughed so hard at the screwed up expression on my immediately beet red face that she cried. And it didn’t help that my pride wouldn’t let me spit out the vinegar missile which had just exploded in my mouth with the power of Tsar Bomba.

And so it was, with my own tears streaming down my cheeks, that I chewed that vinegar Tsar Bomba ... and I chewed .. and I let those tears come ... and my Mom nearly died laughing ... and I finally swallowed down that insane overbearing unforgettable experience.

When Mom stopped laughing she asked me how it was. And when I could speak (large amounts of vinegar do funny things to your mouth), I managed to whisper “That’s not how you make pickles, is it?” And Mom laughed again and said “No honey, that’s not how they make pickles.”

Those spears went down the drain. And I didn’t try making pickles again for years. When I was about 37, I tried again. Found a recipe which seemed pretty basic. Water, sugar, salt, and yes vinegar. My wife thought I was crazy. And the pickles turned out pretty meh.
